get.description: **media.access_key.manage** (first-party): Issue, list and revoke the S3 access keys of a project (ADR-031, amended 2026-10-14: Media issues the keys it verifies). A first-party service (OpenVibe.Zone, OpenVibe.Services) calls for the person in on_behalf_of, who must be an admin or owner of the project (Media asks Network, network.project.member.read). POST /api/v1/projects/:project_id/access-keys takes media.access-key-issue-request@1 and answers 201 media.access-key-issued@1, the only answer that carries the secret; GET lists media.access-key-list@1; DELETE /:key_id revokes at once. Loopback only.

post.summary: Control a media object through OpenVibe.Media's control API (ADR-048, plan T13 step 10): POST /api/v1/resources/control takes one common.resource-control-request@1 naming a media.object by its OVRN, f
post.description: **media.resource.control** (first-party): Control a media object through OpenVibe.Media's control API (ADR-048, plan T13 step 10): POST /api/v1/resources/control takes one common.resource-control-request@1 naming a media.object by its OVRN, from a first-party service (OpenVibe.Services) acting for the person in on_behalf_of. Action: delete (a soft delete, exactly as DELETE /api/v1/objects/:id: the object stops being served at once and can be restored through the API until its retention period ends; an object under a retention hold, or a legacy VOD, clip or file managed through its own routes, is refused). Any other action is refused unsupported. Only the object's owner may act on it, and only inside the project the OVRN names. dry_run decides and explains without applying. The first answer per (caller, project, idempotency_key) is kept and returned for a repeat; the same key with another request is refused. Answers common.resource-control-result@1.

get.summary: Provision a zone in OpenVibe.Media (ADR-031 amendment 2026-10-02), granted only to OpenVibe.Zone: PUT /internal/zones/:zone_id with the zone.object-zone@1 record Zone owns.
get.description: **media.zone.provision** (first-party): Provision a zone in OpenVibe.Media (ADR-031 amendment 2026-10-02), granted only to OpenVibe.Zone: PUT /internal/zones/:zone_id with the zone.object-zone@1 record Zone owns. Media applies a record only when its revision is higher than the one it holds, checks it with contracts.zones.checkObjectZone, and refuses a name another zone of the environment holds (409 media.zone.name_retired) and any change of project, environment, name or namespace (409 media.zone.immutable). Media keeps a projection of each zone to resolve S3 bucket names, enforce the zone's quota_bytes beside the environment's, and answer NoSuchBucket for a zone that is deleting or deleted. GET /internal/zones/:zone_id reports the live objects and, while the zone is deleting, the objects remaining and held; Media tombstones and purges a deleting zone's objects (no restore window) and records when none remain. Loopback only.

common.resource-control-request.v1.title: ResourceControlRequest
common.resource-control-request.v1.description: common.resource-control-request@1: one control operation OpenVibe.Services (or Actor's Console) sends to the authority that owns a resource (ADR-048, plan T13). Services never mutates another service's database; every create, update, start, stop, delete, resize, rotate, pair, grant or revoke is this request to the owning authority's control API, which decides and answers with a common.resource-control-result@1. A request names exactly one of resource (every action but create) or resource_kind (create, before the name exists). project_id is the tenancy boundary and equals the project segment of resource. idempotency_key makes a retry safe: the authority answers a repeated key with the first result. A sensitive action (money, publishing, deleting, physical control) is refused with confirmation_required until its owner approves; the retry carries that confirmation_id (roadmap WS-Z2). The cross-field rules are checked by contracts.resources.checkControlRequest.

resource.description: The resource acted on; required for every action but create.

resource_kind.description: service.type (a common.resource-summary@1 kind), for create, before the resource name exists.

params.description: Action-specific input, shaped by the authority's own contract (never redefined here).

on_behalf_of.description: The subject whose grant the authority checks; the caller's own token says who sent it.

confirmation_id.description: The approved confirmation from an earlier confirmation_required answer.

common.resource-control-result.v1.title: ResourceControlResult
common.resource-control-result.v1.description: common.resource-control-result@1: the authority's answer to a common.resource-control-request@1 (ADR-048, plan T13). state is the outcome, not the resource's own state: done (applied), pending (accepted and asynchronous; the authority reports completion later on its events), refused (a policy or confirmation gate said no) or failed (an error). State rules: refused carries problem or confirmation_required; failed carries problem; done and pending carry neither; confirmation_required appears only on refused. result carries the authority's own response document and never another service's rows. The state rules are checked by contracts.resources.checkControlResult.

confirmation_required.description: The action needs its owner's approval; retry the same request with this confirmation_id once approved.

problem.description: RFC 9457 body when refused or failed.

common.resource-list-result.v1.title: ResourceListResult
common.resource-list-result.v1.description: A page of the resource index (roadmap WS-Z7).

partial.description: Authorities a merged index (OpenVibe.Services, ADR-048) could not read for this page: a slow or failing authority is omitted, never fails the page. Each entry names the authority and the problem code it answered. Added in 1.1.0; a single authority's own index leaves it out.

common.resource-name.v1.title: ResourceName
common.resource-name.v1.description: common.resource-name@1: the one stable, cross-service name of an OpenVibe resource (OVRN; ADR-034 section 2, ADR-048, plan T13): ovrn:<service>:<project_id>:<type>/<id>, for example ovrn:media:prj_01J0000000000000000000000A:object/med_01K0000000000000000000000B. The service segment is the authority that owns the resource; the project segment is its tenancy boundary; type is the second half of a common.resource-summary@1 kind and id is that summary's id, so the name composes from any resource summary. It is used in grant scopes, audit rows, event subjects, usage records, bill lines and console URLs. It never names a person, an app, a request, a session or an event. The pattern is the one common.usage-recorded@1 resource and common.resource-summary@1 ovrn already use.

common.resource-summary.v1.title: ResourceSummary
common.resource-summary.v1.description: One resource of any service, as the resource index lists it (roadmap WS-Z7): every service answers GET /api/v1/resources with these, so OpenVibe.Services shows any resource without owning its data.

kind.description: service.kind, e.g. watch.watch, actor.actor, media.object, events.subscription

ovrn.description: Optional resource name (ADR-034 section 2), the name grants, audit, events, usage records and bills use: ovrn:<service>:<project_id>:<type>/<id>, e.g. ovrn:watch:<project_id>:watch/<wch_id>, with the pattern of common.usage-recorded@1 resource. Its service, project and id are this summary's service, project_id and id. Added in 1.1.0.

errors.problem.v1.title: Problem
errors.problem.v1.description: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a stable OpenVibe error code and trace identifiers. The legacy 'error' string is allowed during migration so existing clients keep working.

error.description: Deprecated compatibility field: same text as title/detail for clients that read {error}.

identity.subject-ref.v1.title: SubjectRef
identity.subject-ref.v1.description: The one cross-platform reference to an actor. Issued by OpenVibe.Network. Never a service-local integer id.

oneOf.description: AgentSubject: an agent (OpenVibe.Actor, or a developer app's agent) acting under grants its owner delegated (roadmap WS-Z2). In an event envelope, on_behalf_of names the owner.

media.access-key-issue-request.v1.title: AccessKeyIssueRequest
media.access-key-issue-request.v1.description: media.access-key-issue-request@1 (ADR-031): the body of POST /api/v1/projects/:project_id/access-keys on OpenVibe.Media (capability media.access_key.manage), sent by a first-party service (OpenVibe.Zone, OpenVibe.Services) for the person in on_behalf_of, who must be an admin or owner of the project (Network decides). The answer is 201 media.access-key-issued@1. A zone that is not an active zone of this project environment answers 404 media.access_key.unknown_zone; more than 50 live keys in one environment answer 409 media.access_key.limit.

media.access-key-issued.v1.title: AccessKeyIssued
media.access-key-issued.v1.description: media.access-key-issued@1 (ADR-031): the 201 of POST /api/v1/projects/:project_id/access-keys. `secret` is the S3 secret access key; it is in this answer only, and Media never shows it again. A caller relays it to the person once and keeps no copy.

media.access-key.v1.title: AccessKey
media.access-key.v1.description: media.access-key@1 (ADR-031, amended 2026-10-14): one S3 access key of OpenVibe.Media's S3 surface (https://s3.openvibe.media). It is bound to one project environment, reads and/or writes, and may be scoped to some zones of that environment (zone.object-zone@1 ids; empty means every zone). Media issues and verifies it: SigV4 needs the secret, so the party that checks signatures keeps it, encrypted, and shows it once (media.access-key-issued@1). The secret is never part of this record. A revoked key is refused at once; a key scoped only to a zone that is deleted is revoked with it. More fields may be added.

name.description: What uses the key, as the person who issued it named it.

zones.description: The zones it may reach; empty = every zone of the environment.

last_used_at.description: The last signed request, to the minute.

media.avatar-ingest-request.v1.title: MediaAvatarIngestRequest
media.avatar-ingest-request.v1.description: media.avatar-ingest-request@1: the body of POST /internal/avatar-ingest on OpenVibe.Media (capability media.avatar.ingest; Network calls it while adopting an avatar a person pointed at somewhere else on the web). Media fetches the URL once through its egress guard (https only, public addresses only, at most 8 MB and 10 s), re-encodes it to a 512×512 WebP and stores it as an unlisted screenshot paste owned by user_id, so no OpenVibe site ever serves or stores a third-party address. Refusals are { ok: false, error } (400 without url or user_id, 422 when the link is not a usable picture).

url.description: The https address of the picture to import.

user_id.description: The account that owns the stored paste.

username.description: Used only for the paste title.

media.avatar-ingest-result.v1.title: MediaAvatarIngestResult
media.avatar-ingest-result.v1.description: media.avatar-ingest-result@1: the answer of POST /internal/avatar-ingest on OpenVibe.Media: { ok: true, slug, url, width, height, bytes } — the unlisted paste holding the re-encoded avatar and its public https://openvibe.media/p/<slug>/screenshot address (always a 512×512 WebP). Refusals are { ok: false, error } (400, 422).

media.file-read-result.v1.title: MediaFileReadResult
media.file-read-result.v1.description: media.file-read-result@1: answers of media.object.read on OpenVibe.Media. GET /api/v1/:app/files/:key → media.file@1 (the file's metadata; 404 when it is not the tenant's); GET /f/:key → the bytes, with Content-Type and Range (a sandbox file only through its signed URL).

media.file-upload.v1.title: MediaFileUpload
media.file-upload.v1.description: media.file-upload@1: the multipart/form-data body of POST /api/v1/:app/files (media.object.upload, namespace :app): one part named `file` with the bytes and its filename and type. The tenant's quota is checked against the bytes; the answer is media.file@1 (201).

file.description: The multipart part named file (filename and Content-Type from the part).

media.file.v1.title: MediaFile
media.file.v1.description: media.file@1: one stored file of a tenant on OpenVibe.Media (server/files/routes.js filePublic): its key, owner, name, size, type and hash, and the URL it is served from (/f/<key>; a developer-project sandbox file gets a short-lived signed URL instead).

media.media-ref.v1.title: MediaRef
media.media-ref.v1.description: Reference to a Media object. Canonical ids (med_<ULID>) arrive with the Wave 4 object model; until then legacy:<app>:<kind>:<id> addresses today's VOD/clip/file/paste/thumbnail rows.

media.object-list.v1.title: MediaObjectList
media.object-list.v1.description: media.object-list@1: a page of GET /api/v2/:app/objects (media.object.list), newest first: the objects the caller may list in the tenant (a Network token sees only the namespaces its grant covers; ?namespace= narrows to one namespace and those below it), without their locations, and the cursor of the next page (null on the last).

media.object.v1.title: MediaObject
media.object.v1.description: media.object@1: one object of the OpenVibe.Media object API v2 (/api/v2/:app/objects; Media server/objects/model.js objectPublic): its id and legacy ref, tenant and namespace (the tenant's root, or a namespace below it), kind, owner, visibility, lifecycle, type, size and hash, readiness, and where it is served. Copies are described by provider and state, never by path or key. More fields may be added.

legacy_ref.description: legacy:<app>:<kind>:<id> for an object projected from a VOD, clip, file or paste row; null for a native v2 object.

app_id.description: The tenant: an app id, or prj_<ULID> / prj_<ULID>-sandbox for a developer project.

namespace.description: The namespace grants name: the tenant's root (its app id; app.<project_id> or app.<project_id>.sandbox for a developer project) or a namespace below it (<root>.<segment>…).

content_hash.description: sha256 hex of the bytes, once known.

held.description: Under a retention hold (its own, or a clip's source VOD's).

public_url.description: Where a public or unlisted ready object is served; null for private and sandbox objects (download signs them).

zone.object-zone.v1.title: ObjectZone
zone.object-zone.v1.description: zone.object-zone@1 (ADR-031 amendment 2026-10-02): one named object zone, as OpenVibe.Zone's control API returns it (GET /api/v1/zones/{zone_id}, the list under /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/zones, and the 201 of a create). Zone owns this record: its name, environment, state, access policy and per-zone quota setting. Media owns everything inside it: the objects (ordinary med_ objects in the namespace media_namespace), their keys, bytes and replicas, quota enforcement, usage counting and the one deletion path. Zone never lists keys or holds bytes. The S3 bucket name is `name`, resolved within the project and environment of the access key that signs the request, at https://s3.openvibe.media/<name>/<key>. `ovrn` is ovrn:zone:<project_id>:object-zone/<id>, with the same project_id and id as this record. The id is never reused, and neither is a name: within one project environment a name belongs to one zone for ever, deleted or not, so a signed request names exactly one zone id. Name and env are immutable. Every environment has exactly one `default` zone, whose media_namespace is the environment root. Zone creates it with the environment, and it cannot be deleted on its own. Its access is per-object, and every other zone's is private. JSON Schema cannot compare fields: contracts.zones.checkObjectZone also requires that ovrn names this project_id and id, and that media_namespace is the environment root of project_id and env, followed by .<id> unless the zone is the default. More fields may be added.

ovrn.description: The resource name used in grants, audit, events, usage records and bills (ADR-034 section 2).

env.description: Fixed at creation. A sandbox key never resolves a production zone.

name.description: The S3 bucket name. It is unique among all the zones of one project environment, deleted ones included: a deleted zone's name is retired, never given to another zone. It is valid as an S3 bucket name.

default.description: The environment's default zone, named `default`. Its media_namespace is the environment root.

access.description: private: every named zone in v1. Its objects never have a public_url and never enter a public cache. per-object: only the default zone, whose existing objects keep their own visibility (public, unlisted or private), public URLs and cached copies, as media.object@1 allows. The S3 surface never serves an object without a signature, in either kind of zone. Publication of a named zone would add a value in a later minor version.

state.description: provisioning: Media has not yet acknowledged the zone. active: it serves requests. deleting: requests answer NoSuchBucket while Media tombstones the objects and erases every copy. deleted: no object or copy remains. The record is kept, and its name stays retired.

media_namespace.description: Where Media keeps the zone's objects. It is the environment root for the default zone, and <root>.<id> for every other zone.

quota_bytes.description: An optional byte ceiling for this zone. Media enforces it together with the project environment's byte quota, and a write over either is refused with QuotaExceeded. null means only the environment quota applies.

usage.description: A snapshot of the live objects, as Media reports it. Zone never counts. Billed usage comes from Media's hourly media.usage.recorded rollups, whose dimension is this id in lowercase.

deletion.description: Progress of a zone deletion, as Media reports it.

objects_remaining.description: Objects not yet tombstoned, plus tombstoned objects with a copy not yet confirmed erased.

held_objects.description: Objects whose erasure waits for a retention hold (ADR-006). They are already unreadable.

revision.description: Raised by every change. Zone sends it when it provisions the change in Media, and Media applies only a higher revision.

openvibeToken.description: An OpenVibe Network token for this service: a person's token, an app token (client credentials, audience of the service) or a first-party service token. Its `cap` claim must include the capability the operation names.
